name: Bet Dwarka (Beyt Dwarka)
location: Bet Dwarka island, Devbhoomi Dwarka, Gujarat
summary: Bet (Beyt) Dwarka — the island temple pilgrims traditionally combine with mainland Dwarkadhish.
famousFor: Island Krishna shrine of the Dwarka yatra
mythology: Bet Dwarka is linked in pilgrimage memory to Krishna’s residence and to the wider Dwarka–Prabhas sacred coast. Boat access and island darshan complete many Gujarat Krishna yatras after the mainland Dwarkadhish temple.

climate: Hot and dry inland; humid on the coast; monsoon mid-year.

mythologySignificance:
Bet Dwarka is linked in pilgrimage memory to Krishna’s residence and to the wider Dwarka–Prabhas sacred coast. Boat access and island darshan complete many Gujarat Krishna yatras after the mainland Dwarkadhish temple.

Classical pilgrimage teaching places Bet Dwarka (Beyt Dwarka) within India’s tirtha network: a location where devotion to Lord Krishna (Dwarkadhish / Bet Dwarka) is believed to ripen vows more readily than in ordinary space. Epic, Puranic, and regional mahatmya literature — not a single uniform text — sustain this sense of sacred geography.
localBeliefs:
In popular pilgrimage memory, Bet Dwarka (Beyt Dwarka) is especially associated with Island Krishna shrine of the Dwarka yatra. Guides and elders retell this identity to first-time visitors as the living ‘reason’ the tirtha draws crowds.

Local sthala-purana and priestly teaching at Bet Dwarka (Beyt Dwarka) elaborate how Lord Krishna (Dwarkadhish / Bet Dwarka) blesses devotees who arrive with vows, gratitude, or grief. Festival days intensify these beliefs through processions, special alankara, and community feeding where practised.

Pilgrims commonly link practical customs — dress, queue, prasadam, and parikrama — with spiritual fruit. Such customs are living belief: they vary by region and should be followed as posted by the temple trust or endowment board.
